stories.headline: Fantasy buzz: Week 11's leading fantasy scorers through Sunday's early games
stories.summary: A closer look at the top 10 fantasy scorers in Week 11, including Cowboys QB Dak Prescott and Broncos RB Jonah Coleman.
stories.body:
Several Dallas Cowboys and Kansas City Chiefs were among Week 11's leading fantasy scorers, with Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb and Travis Kelce all in the top five. And then there was Denver Broncos rookie Jonah Coleman, who found the end zone three times against the Las Vegas Raiders.

Javonte Williams and George Pickens joined in on the fun in the Cowboys' 21-point rout of Tennessee, while Patrick Mahomes and Emmett Johnson were the other Chiefs to crack the top 10 in the team's easy win over Arizona.

Here's the complete list of the top 10 fantasy scorers for Week 11.

1. Dak Prescott, QB, Dallas Cowboys -- 35.9

2. Jonah Coleman, RB, Denver Broncos -- 34.9

3. CeeDee Lamb, WR, Dallas Cowboys -- 30.2

4. Ashton Jeanty, RB, Las Vegas Raiders -- 27.9

5. Jahmyr Gibbs, RB, Detroit Lions -- 27.8

6. Chuba Hubbard, RB, Carolina Panthers -- 26.0

7. Travis Kelce, TE, Kansas City Chiefs -- 25.4

8. Patrick Mahomes, QB, Kansas City Chiefs -- 24.96

9. Emmett Johnson, RB, Kansas City Chiefs -- 24.3

10. Javonte Williams, RB, Dallas Cowboys -- 24.1

Nov. 20: Jones released; Richardson Sr. takes over as starter

With the Indianapolis Colts releasing Daniel Jones, the team will start Anthony Richardson Sr. for the Week 12 matchup versus the New York Giants. So, let's quickly discuss how this impacts the Colts offense from a fantasy perspective.

Richardson brings big-time, dual-threat upside as a runner, as he has posted 640 yards rushing and 10 touchdowns in 19 career games in the league. We should see Richardson's rushing ability used in the Colts' game plan, with more designed carries mixed into the call sheet. However, with a lack of current wide receiver talent in Indy, plus Richardson's accuracy concerns (50.8% career completion rate), he will be a mid-to-lower tier QB2 in my rankings.

Running back Jonathan Taylor, who has scored fewer than 10 points in three of his last four games, could get a slight bump with Richardson as the starter if we get a more run-heavy approach from the Colts, one that also creates cutback lanes and misdirection off the QB read schemes. However, Richardson can also be deployed as a runner near the goal line, which would take away scoring opportunities from Taylor. And I don't see Taylor getting a bump in receiving volume here. Taylor will remain as an RB2 in my rankings simply due to the anticipated rushing volume.

Tight end Tyler Warren scored only 3.2 fantasy points in the Thursday night loss to the Texans (catching one pass for 22 yards), his fourth straight game with fewer than 10 points. Maybe we will see Warren deployed more on seams, corners and third-level throws due to the arm talent of Richardson, but Warren averages only 5.05 air yards per target this season. Until we see the Colts actually cater to the receiving traits of Warren, a quarterback change isn't going to put him back into the TE1 conversation.

-- Matt Bowen

Nov. 20: How should fantasy managers approach the Rams?

With reports of Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua being sidelined for two months after knee surgery, which is the remainer of the fantasy football season, let's discuss how managers should approach Sean McVay's pass game moving forward.

As this offense currently sits, I don't see a Rams pass catcher that needs to be in lineups until Davante Adams (hamstring) returns from IR. As we saw last week, with Nacua out, the Rams used multiple tight ends in their system, one that leaned on the run game. And Matthew Stafford spread the ball around, as nine players caught at least one pass, with wide receiver Konata Mumpfield and tight end Tyler Higbee both grabbing a team-high three receptions.

Once Adams is healthy, and back in the mix, he will have WR1 value, but until then, this is a pass game by committee in L.A., which keeps Stafford in the QB2 range for the Week 12 matchup versus the Green Bay Packers.

-- Matt Bowen

Nov. 20: Stroud shining bright in Houston, Colts continue to crumble

It feels fitting that the Houston Texans were wearing uniforms on Thursday night that paid homage to those great Oilers teams of the past, conjuring images of some of those great "Luv Ya Blue" quarterbacks of old. We're talking the Warren Moons, Steve McNairs and Kenny Stablers of the world.

Yes, on the off chance that you know who Ken Stabler is, you might be shocked to find out he was once a member of a team called the Houston Oilers. Sure, I could have gone with Dan Pastorini, but I've been told before that I tend to lose you by going more obscure with the history.

I only bring this up because this version of the Texans is a lot more fun than they have any right to be -- if you can call Thursday's game fun. Houston won in a blowout, which was a surprise to nobody except for me as I talked myself into thinking the Indianapolis Colts would keep it close because divisional games on Thursday night tend to be closer than people think. Of course, I also think Metallica was truly at its best during the Cliff Burton era, so what do I know? Again, obscure. Stopping now.

The biggest takeaway from this very much not-so-close game? C.J. Stroud. He was good again, finishing with three touchdowns in his fifth consecutive game with multiple TDs. Stroud is now a must-start quarterback every week, even in a game where many of you (and definitely not me) expected a blowout, he still racked up a ton of fantasy points. There is no quarterback I would start over him beyond the usual suspects. It's been a tremendous transformation for Stroud, who started the season as "extremely ordinary" and is now extraordinary.

Here are a few more notes from Thursday night:

My guy David Montgomery is back! It's not a moment too soon, with "Bye-mageddon" having arrived this week. He ran the ball 26 times for 107 yards, his first 100-yard game since Week 3 of last season when he was playing for the Detroit Lions. Needless to say, there were no concerns about "easing him back" or "putting him on a pitch count" in this one. He's a solid RB2 moving forward, with the Baltimore Ravens, Pittsburgh Steelers and Washington Commanders as his next three opponents. Up first are the Ravens, who are middle-of-the-road against running backs and have allowed 14 rushing scores this season.
Nico Collins has TD receptions in three consecutive games. He was kind of bailed out by that touchdown grab because his receiving numbers have been ... fine. It's getting to the point where the Texans might have too many options at receiver. And don't forget how the Texans love to throw touchdowns to random tight ends, too. I mean Marlin Klein scored a touchdown this week. MARLIN KLEIN!!! You're not benching Collins, but we also wouldn't mind a huge performance from him one of these weeks.
I don't know what to do about any of the Colts. Seth McGowan went down with an injury and didn't return in the second half. Jonathan Taylor looks lost out there. I haven't seen a JT want to get away from his group this bad since Justin Timberlake was trying to leave 98 Degrees. I'm kidding. I know JT was a member of the Backstreet Boys. Give me some credit. Still, I'm not sure what we can realistically expect from any of the Colts for the rest of the season.

-- Adam Rank

Nov. 19: 11 key fantasy football stats for Week 11

We're officially in Week 11 of the NFL season, and fantasy playoffs are right around the corner. In order to make the best lineup decisions to make sure managers are maximizing their rosters for that final playoff push, here's 11 of my favorite fantasy stats so far this season.

1. Baltimore Ravens TE Mark Andrews had his best game of the season in his first game with Jacoby Brissett starting at QB. He turned eight targets into eight catches for 82 yards and 16.2 fantasy points, all of which were season highs. Brissett has thrown 14% of his passes to tight ends since 2022, much higher than the league-average rate of 11%. That number would be even higher if not for Trey McBride running such a high percentage of his routes from the slot. Brissett elevates tight ends and a fantasy resurgence could be underway for Andrews.

2. Jacksonville Jaguars WR Parker Washington leads the NFL in yards against man coverage (262) while Trevor Lawrence is fifth in the NFL in yards per attempt against man coverage (8.4). This week they get the New York Giants, who play man at the fifth-highest rate in the NFL (32%), which sets up what could be another big week for the duo.

3. Seattle Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba currently has picked up 52% of his team's receiving yards. Not only is that the most in the Next Gen Stats era (since 2016), there has only been one other season where a player recorded over 40% of their teams receiving yards: Smith-Njigba in 2025, when he picked up 44%. If there was ever a season for a wide receiver to win MVP, JSN is having it.

4. The "something's got to give" matchup of the week is Brock Purdy against the Minnesota Vikings defense. Minnesota blitzes a league-high 72% of the time (the next closest is 44%) and a QB hasn't scored more than 13 fantasy points against them since Week 1. Purdy leads the league in touchdowns (12), passer rating and yards per attempt against the blitz.

5. Vikings WR Justin Jefferson saw 13 targets in his first game back with Kirk Cousins. That is the most targets he has had in any game since 2024's Week 16. He saw 11 of those targets against zone coverage, and this week he gets the San Francisco 49ers, who play zone at the second-highest rate in the NFL (87%).

6. QB Cam Ward has thrown at least 39 times in each of the last two games, scoring 26.26 and 19.14 fantasy points. In fact, he has thrown multiple passing TDs in two straight games, something he did not do in any of the first seven games. He gets a chance to stay hot against the Dallas Cowboys defense, who are top four in passing TDs allowed and QB fantasy PPG.

7. Los Angeles Chargers RB Omarion Hampton has played on over 60% of snaps just twice this season, going for 115 and 105 rushing yards (respectively) with a touchdown in each. Hampton has an excellent chance to keep producing against the New York Jets, who have allowed the second-most rushing yards per game (116) and rush yards before contact per attempt (1.6) to RBs.

8. New Orleans Saints WR Jordyn Tyson saw elite usage in his first NFL game with no limitations. He saw 13 targets, which is good for a 38% target share and 50% air yard share. He split his time out wide (50%) and in the slot (45%). He has league-winner potential on the team that throws at the fifth-highest rate. He should be (at worst) a WR3 for fantasy.

9. Kansas City Chiefs WR Josh Downs only played on 10 snaps in his debut and he still saw five targets, catching four of them for 53 yards, a touchdown and 15.3 fantasy points -- his best fantasy performance of the season. All 10 came from the slot, where Patrick Mahomes throws 28% of his passes. There is a lot of fantasy potential here.

10. Buffalo Bills QB Josh Allen is currently on pace for 25 passing and 21 rushing touchdowns. That would be the first 20-20 season in NFL history. There have been two 20-15 seasons in NFL history: Allen (29 passing, 15 rushing TDs) and Jalen Hurts (23 passing, 15 rushing), both in 2023.

11. Cincinnati Bengals QB Joe Burrow is on pace for 5,279 passing yards and 51 touchdowns. The only QB to ever top those numbers in a season was Peyton Manning in 2013 (5,477 yards, 55 TDs).

-- Michael F. Florio

Nov. 18: Reliable lineup locks to target in trades, Knockout leagues

As an avid fan of -- and our primary ranker for -- our new Knockout fantasy football game this season, I'm all about the consistency kings.

(On an aside, it's a great week to join a new Knockout league, being that you need only eight managers to play!)

Sure, those win-your-matchup-all-by-himself scores from George Pickens, Jordan Love or Tee Higgins the past three weeks are plenty of fun. But bolstering your lineup with the "old reliables" is important, too, and that's especially so in a game where avoiding a low statistical floor is paramount.

That's why last week's trade which sent veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders to the Minnesota Vikings piqued my interest. Cousins is tied for the fourth-most games as a top-10 fantasy quarterback this season (five), but he has also been the most consistent player at his position. Aside from his five top-10 weeks, Cousins' other games saw him finish 11th, 17th, 18th, 19th and 21st, and in only three of those was his score more than five points beneath the No. 10 score.

Best yet, you can surely get Cousins for a song in trade, being that he has exceeded the one-third (33.3%) start rate in ESPN leagues only once all season (in Week 6), and sits at only 65.1% rostered today. He fits, almost perfectly, the mold of the old-reliable backup/weekly superflex quarterback. To that end, in a freshly drafting Knockout league of mine Tuesday night, my No. 1 quarterback target was Trevor Lawrence -- more on that in a moment -- but my backup was Cousins. It's a pairing that will bring much comfort at a discounted price from many of the other name brands.

Cousins' reliability also benefits his receivers, who warrant trade inquiries as well. Justin Jefferson's best seasons came with Cousins under center, and Jordan Addison's thumb surgery, which is expected to cost him multiple weeks, locks Jefferson into the alpha role in Minnesota. Jefferson had a season-high 13 targets and 16.4 fantasy points in Cousins' return, which bolstered Jefferson's fantasy WR1 status. Tight end T.J. Hockenson should also benefit from Cousins' installation and Addison's absence.

To put a bow on it, the Vikings have the second-most-favorable remaining schedule for quarterbacks, and the fifth-most favorable for wide receivers.

Cousins and his Vikings teammates, aren't the only ones on my consistency-oriented trade target list. Here are two others:

Bhayshul Tuten, RB, Jacksonville Jaguars: I'm all-in on the Jaguars in fantasy, as they're on an unreal run over the past year, and they match up brilliantly, schedule-wise, down the stretch. It's the reason for my Lawrence interest in Tuesday's draft, but when examining an offense likely to remain on a roll, the running back is certainly someone you want. Tuten's 56% rushing share is 13th at the position, and only 14 running backs have delivered a top-25 "start worthy" score more often. In a season of injury-driven fantasy lineup volatility, he's a "set it and forget it" weekly RB2.

Stefon Diggs, WR, Washington Commanders: He's a ho-hum type, started in greater than 40% of ESPN leagues only three times all season, but someone has to catch passes in Washington. Diggs has a 20% target rate for the season, and he's tied for 11th among wide receivers in top-25 fantasy weeks. Antonio Williams might be the exciting, high-ceiling receiver in the Commanders' offense, but there's Diggs week after week, delivering his 10-15 points to his fantasy managers. Also be aware that the Commanders have the position's fourth-most-favorable remaining schedule.

-- Tristan H. Cockcroft

stories.headline: Tage Thompson scores twice as Sabres top Lightning, 6-2
stories.summary: — Tage Thompson scored twice, Zach Benson had a goal and two assists and Ukka-Pekka Luukkonen finished with 29 saves and the Buffalo Sabres beat the Tampa Bay Lightning 6-2 on Sunday.
stories.body:
TAMPA, Fla. -- — Tage Thompson scored twice, Zach Benson had a goal and two assists and Ukka-Pekka Luukkonen finished with 29 saves and the Buffalo Sabres beat the Tampa Bay Lightning 6-2 on Sunday.


Noah Ostlund had a goal and two points. Jack Quinn and Jiri Kulich also scored for Buffalo.


The Sabres won for the second time in the past eight games.


Nikita Kucherov and Gage Goncalves scored for Tampa Bay, which suffered only its second loss on home ice this season in 12 games (10-2-0). Dennis Hildeby finished with 22 saves to suffer his first regulation loss this season in his sixth start.


Thompson has goals in four consecutive games and 12 goals in his past 12 games. His 33rd career multi-goal game ties Pat LaFontaine for 10th most in franchise history.


Thompson's two goals 5:12 apart in the second period broke open the game for Buffalo. He scored on a one-timer from the left circle for a 5-on-3 power play goal for a 3-1 lead then danced around Pontus Holmberg, who lost his stick, to get to the middle slot for a wrist shot at 16:17.


It was the 18th multi-goal period for Thompson, tying Dave Andreychuk for fifth most in franchise history.


Quinn increased his goal-scoring streak to three games, converting a 2-on-1 chance 1:22 into the second period to break a 1-1 tie.


Goncalves notched his first of the season to bring the Lightning to within 4-2 at 5:50 of the third period, but Ostlund put Buffalo back ahead by three goals a minute later. Benson added an empty net goal with 1:09 left.


Up next
Sabres: Host New York Rangers on Wednesday


Lightning: Host Carolina on Wednesday


------

stories.headline: Sources: Mets, Skubal agree to record 9-year, $450M contract
stories.summary: Tarik Skubal and the Mets agreed to a nine-year, $450 million contract, sources told ESPN. It is the richest deal for a pitcher, both by total and average annual value.
stories.body:
Two-time Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal and the New York Mets are in agreement on a nine-year, $450 million contract, sources told ESPN's Jeff Passan on Sunday.

It is the richest deal ever for a pitcher, both by total value and average annual value ($50 million).

Skubal is set to join a club that was thirsty for a clear-cut No. 1 starter to partner with promising right-hander Nolan McLean atop its rotation after missing the postseason in consecutive years despite carrying one of the top two most expensive payrolls in the majors.

The Mets were considered the favorites all along to land Skubal with Steve Cohen, the richest owner in baseball, fueling their push. They ultimately beat out the Toronto Blue Jays, San Diego Padres and Los Angeles Dodgers to land the top player in free agency.

Skubal made his decision after meeting with each team in California last week.

The Dodgers never got to a point where they made Skubal an offer, sources told ESPN's Alden Gonzalez. They wanted him back, and were willing to ultimately go long term, but the uncertainty of a new collective bargaining agreement and what the economic model might look like prevented them from doing so pre-lockout.

The deal sets the all-time mark for guaranteed money for a pitcher, which had been $325 million by Yoshinobu Yamamoto, over 12 years (Dodgers, 2023), while the AAV record for a pitcher had been $43.3 million, set by Max Scherzer (Mets, 2021).

The agreement is a departure from Mets president of baseball operations David Stearns' approach to not giving long-term contracts to free agent starting pitchers in their late 20s and early 30s.

The Mets pursued Yamamoto, then 25, during Stearns' first winter in charge after the 2024 season and offered him a long-term deal. Yamamoto, however, wound up signing the record deal with the Dodgers.

Before Skubal's deal, the longest contract that Stearns had given to a free agent starting pitcher was for three years.

Skubal's contract isn't even the richest one on the Mets' books. That belongs to Juan Soto, another Scott Boras client who signed another record-breaking 15-year, $765 million contract in December 2024.

The Mets currently have seven players on the books with at least an AAV of $20 million next season -- Soto, Skubal, Bo Bichette, Francisco Lindor, Marcus Semien, Sean Manaea and Jorge Polanco.

The team's projected payroll for next season is already over $340 million, according to Cot's Baseball Contracts.

The historic expenditure comes in the midst of a labor war in which owners are pushing a salary cap for the first time since 1994, a demand that led to a player strike that lasted more than seven months and the cancellation of a World Series for the first time in 90 years. The owners had stayed away from proposing a salary cap in subsequent negotiations -- and the league, outside of the COVID-shortened 2020 season, has avoided missing games.

This time, however, the owners have decided to disturb the labor peace for their coveted salary cap. They are expected to impose a lockout when the current CBA expires on Dec. 1. The MLB Players Association maintains it will not accept a salary cap. An ugly battle is expected to not only threaten the start of the 2027 season, but perhaps the entire season.

When the season does start, the Mets will have one of the game's best pitchers on their side. Skubal, who turned 30 on Nov. 20, is a bona fide ace who has been every bit as dominant as he has been durable. Over the past three seasons, Skubal ranks third among starters in ERA (2.42), second in strikeouts (655), fourth in innings (546) and first in FanGraphs wins above replacement (18).

Since 2023, Skubal has made 103 starts with a 2.47 ERA and 757 strikeouts. His ERA is the lowest among 39 MLB pitchers with at least 100 starts during that span and more than a half-run lower than the next-closest qualifiers, Cristopher Sanchez (2.97) and Zack Wheeler (2.98), according to ESPN Research.

A ninth-round pick by the Detroit Tigers out of Seattle University in 2018, Skubal began to emerge as a front-line starter in 2023 and took it to another level thereafter, winning back-to-back American League Cy Young Awards in 2024 and 2025, the first of which came unanimously.

With free agency approaching, the left-hander was the subject of trade rumors after the 2025 season and won a high-stakes fight over his 2026 compensation in February, when an independent arbitrator ruled in favor of his side's proposal ($32 million) over that of the Tigers' front office ($19 million).

Rather than trade Skubal, the Tigers splurged on another rotation anchor in Framber Valdez and doubled down on their efforts to win the American League Central. But a slew of injuries and a 6-22 month of May ultimately gave president of baseball operations Scott Harris little choice but to put Skubal on the trade market near the end of July. The Dodgers ultimately beat out the Milwaukee Brewers and others, landing him with a prospect package headlined by outfielder Zyhir Hope and right-hander River Ryan.

Skubal posted a 2.61 ERA in 10 starts for the Dodgers in August and September -- plus another 11 innings of three-run ball in October -- and finished 12-7 with a 2.72 ERA over 158⅔ innings for the season. It was Skubal's lowest innings total in three years, but his workload would have been a lot smaller if not for a revolutionary procedure by Dr. Neal ElAttrache, who used a nanoneedle to perform a less invasive surgery to remove loose bodies from his elbow and essentially cut his recovery time in half.

It helped put Skubal and Boras on a path to eventually secure a record contract.

stories.headline: Cincinnati stuns Shield-winners Nashville to start best-of-3 series
stories.summary: Roman Celentano made six saves for his fourth clean sheet of the season as FC Cincinnati took advantage of an early own goal to earn a 1-0 victory over Nashville SC on Sunday.
stories.body:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. -- Roman Celentano made six saves for his fourth clean sheet of the season as FC Cincinnati took advantage of an early own goal to earn a 1-0 victory over Nashville SC on Sunday to begin a best-of-three series.

Cincinnati needs one more win to knock out the Supporters' Shield winner -- and MLS single-season points record holder -- with Game 2 scheduled for Saturday.

Nashville lost its first home match of the season after entering 15-0-2 in MLS play at GEODIS Park and outscoring opponents 48-14. Nashville is looking to become the ninth Supporters' Shield winner to win the MLS Cup in the league's 31-year history.

Cincinnati took the lead in the seventh minute. Nashville midfielder Patrick Yazbek came under pressure and tried to play it back to goalkeeper Brian Schwake, who was out of his area, but inadvertently curled into the back of his own net.

Cincinnati appeared to go ahead 2-0 in the 11th minute after a corner kick, but the glancing header was disallowed for a questionable foul in the box.

Nashville had several scoring chances in the second half. Hany Mukhtar had a shot deflect off the crossbar in the 63rd. Then, Sam Surridge appeared to score in the 75th, but Mukhtar was caught offside.

Celentano denied Mukhtar's close-range attempt in the 81st.

B.J. Callaghan's Nashville side set league records for points (77), wins (23), home wins (15), goals conceded (25), and fewest losses (three) this season. Nashville also tied the MLS record with 17 clean sheets and allowed just 25 goals, the fewest in the modern era of MLS.

stories.headline: Way-too-early look ahead to the 2027 AFL Draft: 15 players to know
stories.summary: The 2027 AFL Draft will look markedly different to the past few years with the introduction of Tasmania. Who are the players to know? Jasper Chellappah has named 15 to keep an eye on next year.
stories.body:
On to the next.

The 2027 AFL Draft will look markedly different to the past few years, with Tasmania's inclusion making for an expansion draft similar to that of 2010 and 2011. The Devils own picks 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, and 13 in the first round, plus the first pick of each subsequent round as part of concessions.

The club will need to trade 5, 7, 11, and 13 or roll them into 2028 or 2029. That means the competition's 19th team will take 1, 3 and 9 to the draft next year.

Tasmania has also pre-listed some of the brightest talents in the crop. Axel Walsh, Baxter Sruk, and Jake Miller were all clear pick No. 1 contenders 12 months out from their draft, and will attend school in Hobart and play football in the VFL next year.

Five Tasmania-tied teens have been included in the ones to watch next year. Another three are club-tied, making 2027 the most compromised draft in AFL history. Twenty-three of the 46 prospects in the AFL Futures exhibition on Grand Final day were club-tied.

Perhaps the saving grace for 18 other clubs is the fact that 2027 has been touted as an elite draft class for some time. There's premium talent still in the open pool and another 12 months for more quality to emerge, with a heavy leaning towards midfielders.

With an extended 15 prospects given the club-tied nature of the class, this is ESPN's way-too-early look ahead to the best prospects in the 2027 AFL Draft.

1. Axel Walsh (Tasmania pre-list)

East Perth/Western Australia

RUC, 201cm

Another in the resurgence of premium ruck prospects in the draft, and perhaps the best. Walsh is a monster in the air; his best traits come with his aerial strength where he drifts back to intercept mark, pushes forward to stretch defences and dominates around the ground. He will fill out to become a true ruck size and is as close to Max Gawn as a prospect has been this decade. Walsh would be the pick one favourite if he wasn't pre-listed by Tasmania.

2. Baxter Sruk (Tasmania pre-list)

Eastern Ranges/Vic Metro

MID, 185cm

Sruk has been a big game performer and consistent midfield standout in the Talent League. He's a physical on-baller that throws his weight around, impacts with his ball-winning and gets forward to kick goals in bunches. Sruk thrives in the heat of the contest and brings tenacity to Tasmania's list.

3. Jake Miller (Tasmania pre-list)

Western Jets/Vic Metro

FWD, 197cm

Miller is the leading key forward prospect next year. He enjoyed a stellar national championships as a bottom-ager, named to the All-Australian team as well as the Talent League All-Australian side. Miller is a brilliant mark with arms outstretched, able to take big contested marks in packs and secure the ball on long searching leads. He's a reliable set shot off his left foot and is an elite runner for his size. Tasmania has already pre-listed the immense talent.

4. Max Thompson

Bendigo Pioneers/Vic Country

FWD/MID, 175cm

Thompson has played in varying positions and looked good but is clearly at his best inside 50. He's smart and crafty, puts speed on the game and is a wonderfully fluid kick of the ball. Thompson can get up the ground and beat his man back to goals, distribute off halfback or win his own ball. He's the type of versatile small forward that clubs will covet.

5. James Artemis

East Fremantle/Western Australia

MID, 177cm

A leading contender in the open pool, Artemis is the cousin of Essendon's Jaxon and will have suitors very early in the draft. He's a hard-nosed contested midfielder that can then link up transition with hard running and slick ball use. He's dogged with the ball up for grabs and then powers through contact to get it moving forward.

6. Koby Bewick (Essendon father-son)

Calder Cannons/Vic Metro

MID, 178cm

Modern footy suits Bewick down to the ground. The son of 1993 and 2000 premiership small forward Darren, the Calder midfielder has been thrown around in different positions but has all the traits to become an excellent on-baller. He's incisive with his movement and foot skills on the outside, and possesses the running base and work ethic to rack up a lot of the ball in transition. He comes alive in open space where he can run and carry and pick out targets inside 50, which could see him start his career off halfback or a wing. Bewick kicked two goals from 19 touches in his Futures outing.

7. Zemes Pilot (Port Adelaide NGA)

South Adelaide/South Australia

FWD/MID, 193cm

Pilot is an elite basketball talent as well, so it's a coup for footy that the 193cm forward is opting to pursue opportunities in Port's NGA. The uber-athletic tall forward is incredible to watch, soaring above packs to take epic marks, breaking ankles with sharp agility and kicking goals from ridiculous angles. He had a game last year in the SANFL U16s with 27 disposals and 9.4 in front of goals.

8. Jett Flower

Eastern Ranges/Vic Metro

MID/DEF, 183cm

Flower is the grandson of Melbourne legend Robbie, and one of the top open pool prospects in 2027. Boasting one of the best names to come through the pathways in some time, Flower is a classy outside midfielder with beautiful foot skills and a strong running base. He likely appeals to clubs as a rebounder out of defence with his competitiveness a feature behind the ball. Flower was best afield in the Futures game with 17 disposals and a goal.

9. Louis Salopek (Port Adelaide father-son)

Dandenong Stingrays/Vic Country

MID/FWD, 186cm

A genuine star of the crop, Salopek has been in the wars across the past year or so, enduring three separate incidents of a collapsed lung. He burst onto the scene for Vic Country in the U16s champs and plays with a high motor, tackling and pressuring through the midfield and pushing forward to hit the scoreboard. He's keen to get to the Power as the son of Steven.

10. Riley Stratford (Tasmania pre-list)

Sandringham Dragons/Vic Metro

MID, 188cm

A taller midfielder who still needs to build into his frame, Stratford has been part of some massive games in his junior career. He was a star for Brighton Grammar on the way to an inaugural APS title and can play on a wing or through the engine room with impact in the air. Tasmania has locked him away and he'll play for their VFL side next year.

11. Oscar Henwood

Gippsland Power/Vic Country

MID, 185cm

Henwood was a key contributor in the Power's Talent League flag and plays with great composure. He can try to bite off too much with his time in possession but is typically creative and uses it really well in space.

12. Harvey Chapman

Sturt/South Australia

DEF, 195cm

Chapman is the lone key defender inside the top bracket of the draft 12 months out, though he plays a more natural role as a rebounder. The SA tall is an excellent kick and sets up play from the last line of defence with instructive ball use. He can intercept with his reading of the play and gets involved in attack up the field.

13. Sam Husband (Tasmania Academy)

Tasmania Devils/Allies

MID, 180cm

The Devils didn't pre-list Husband because they have priority access to Tasmanian in the draft. He's the premier Tassie prospect in their inaugural draft and will be the poster boy of local talent for the 19th team. He's already played two seasons of Talent League football and is at his best using his evasiveness and skills around stoppages.

14. Campbell Creyk

West Perth/Western Australia

MID, 182cm

Creyk surged into the first round mix this year as a contested beast through the midfield. He rips the ball out of stoppages and doesn't often lose one-on-ones, playing with a hard edge that will serve him well at the next level. He will need to round out his game on the outside to continue pushing up draft boards.

15. Taj Garrett

Sturt/South Australia

MID, 183cm

A hard-running midfielder, Garrett's thirst to find the ball and work to contests is an important facet of his game. He outworks opponents and gets forward of the ball to impact. He may play his best football off a wing in the AFL but will get ample exposure on-ball for Sturt next year.

stories.headline: Haas confirm Rafa Camara will finish 2026 season with the team
stories.summary: Brazilian driver Rafa Camara will complete the 2026 season with Haas ahead of his full rookie season in 2027, the team confirmed on Sunday.
stories.body:
Brazilian driver Rafa Camara will complete the 2026 season with Haas ahead of his full rookie season in 2027, the team confirmed on Sunday.

Formula 2 championship leader Camara took the place of ousted Esteban Ocon in Brazil and continued in the seat at this week's Las Vegas Grand Prix.

He will race for the team in Qatar on Nov. 29 and Abu Dhabi on Dec. 6. The Ferrari junior had already been confirmed to be replacing Ocon in 2027, but the Frenchman's sudden sacking during the Mexico City Grand Prix accelerated his F1 debut.

Haas' decision will likely cost Camara the chance to be F2 champion. F1's main feeder series will finish its own championship four races spread across the schedule in Qatar and Abu Dhabi -- Camara holds a slender seven-point lead over Red Bull junior Nikola Tsolov, with Alpine junior Alex Dunne 18 points back.

Team boss Aayo Komatsu said the opportunity for Camara to embed further into the team was too good to turn down. "We're excited to be able to finish the season with Rafa driving and build on his first two race starts with the team in Brazil and America," Komatsu said.

"I'm delighted that Rafa's embraced every track session as a learning opportunity and embedded himself further within the team. We now get to finish the season together which is advantageous to all of us ahead of a relatively short off-season and as our 2027 preparations get underway."

Haas had one other option if they had wanted Camara to finish off his F2 campaign -- reserve driver Ryo Hirakawa filled in for Ocon in Mexico City and scored a top-ten finish on his debut.

- Verstappen mocks George Russell in brutal outburst: 'So far below my level'

Camara will keep driving alongside fellow Ferrari junior Oliver Bearman in the final races. Although it is expected to be completed soon, Bearman has not had a new Haas deal confirmed yet.

Bearman is understood to be in talks with Ferrari about their wider plans for his career, mindful of what happens with him should Lewis Hamilton extend his stay with the team beyond 2027.

stories.headline: DiBernardo joins Rapinoe, Pulisic in pantheon of great Olimpicos
stories.summary: Vanessa DiBernardo joined an elite list on Saturday, scoring for Kansas City direct from a corner. Known in soccer circles as an Olimpico, here are some of the very best.
stories.body:
(Editor's note: This article was originally published on Oct. 2, 2025, and it has been updated after Vanessa DiBernardo's stunner in Saturday's NWSL championship finale.)

For a relatively simple sport, soccer is filled with novelties.

Outfield players don the gloves and go into goal when there's no other option, penalty takers attempt chipped "Panenka" spot kicks to varying degrees of success, goalkeepers sprint the length of the pitch to come up for last-minute corners -- and sometimes they even score. And every now and then, players will score directly from a corner kick.

Highly improbable, sometimes intentional, a goal scored in this way is known as a Gol Olimpico, an Olympic goal.

But how did these goals get their name? The history of the Olimpico is irrevocably intertwined with South American football and with one of its great rivalries: Uruguay vs. Argentina.

- New Premier League record set with eight injury-time goals

- From World Cup Willie to Ciao: Ranking every World Cup mascot

- NWSL has more money than ever, yet its biggest problems remain

On June 9, 1924, Uruguay won the Olympic gold medal in Paris after defeating Switzerland 3-0. Around the same time in June 1924, the International Football Association Board (IFAB) changed the laws around corner kicks, making goals scored directly from the corner legal. But it wasn't until Oct. 2, 1924, that these two pieces of information would combine to create the Olimpico moniker.

Following Uruguay's Olympic victory, they played a two-game friendly series with their South American neighbors Argentina. The teams played out a 1-1 draw in Montevideo in late-September before travelling to Buenos Aires.

The return match was suspended after four minutes due to the large crowd on the sideline and was rescheduled for Oct. 2. Argentina would eventually win the rematch 2-1, but the whole game was filled with controversy. La Celeste withdrew from the match with four minutes remaining and both sides accused the other of excessive aggression.

But the important part of this story happened in the 15th minute, when Argentina's Cesareo Onzari whipped in a corner and scored.

The audacity of the goal and La Albiceleste defeating the Olympic champions was the catalyst for local journalists to dub the goal an Olympic one. From then on, whenever other goals were scored in this fashion, they were described as like the one scored against the Olympians, and soon the label Gol Olimpico was applied to all such goals.

The Olimpico is stunning when it's intentional and sometimes comical when it's not. It really has no right to work considering where players are standing on the field, how much of the target they can see from that position and what they need to do to the ball to make it curve into the back of the net. Whether they dribble through at the near post or sail past everyone into the far corner, there's beauty in the curl of ball, the audacity, the incredulity. It's glorious.

Take Vanessa DiBernardo's opening goal in Saturday's NWSL championship game. The Kansas City Current were set on course for their first NWSL title thanks to DiBernardo's Olimpico in the 54th minute, with the ball curling over everyone's head to nestle into the far corner of the next.

From regular-season matches to finals, the Olympics and even the World Cup, here are some of the very best Olimpicos.

Vanessa DiBernardo, Kansas City Current vs. Washington Spirit | 2026 NWSL championship

Kansas City fans will never forget how the Current's first NWSL championship was secured thanks in large part to DiBernado's kick from the corner. Hang it in the Louvre.

Marcos Coll, Colombia vs. USSR | 1962 World Cup

The most impressive part of the first Olimpico to be scored at a World Cup is who Coll beat in the USSR goal: the legendary Lev Yashin.

Megan Rapinoe, United States vs. Canada | 2012 London Olympics

When it comes to scoring an Olimpico at the Olympics, only one player in soccer history has managed the feat: USWNT icon Rapinoe.

Elise Kellond-Knight, Australia vs. Norway | 2019 Women's World Cup

The Matildas may have got knocked out of the 2019 Women's World Cup on penalties, but they'll always have Kellond-Knight's amazing Olimpico at the Allianz Riviera in Nice.

Leandro Carvalho, Ceará vs. Corinthians | 2019-20 Brazilian Serie A

Carvalho's Olimpico was cunning and spectacular, catching the defence sleeping and using the outside of his foot. What's more, it was scored in the 92nd minute to level the scores at 2-2 against São Paulo giants Corinthians.

Megan Rapinoe, United States vs. Australia | 2020 Tokyo Olympics

Remember when we said that Rapinoe was the only player in soccer history to score an Olimpico at the Olympic Games? Well she's did it twice, repeating her 2012 stunner over eight years later in Tokyo.

Hakan Çalhanoglu, Internazionale vs. AS Roma | 2020-21 Serie A

Why is Çalhanoglu's goal against AS Roma -- in Rome -- so memorable? It's an Olimpico at the Stadio Olimpico of course! How good.

Kyra Cooney-Cross, Melbourne Victory vs. Sydney FC | 2020-21 A-League Women

In the 120th minute of the A-League Women Grand Final, 19-year-old Cooney-Cross stepped up to take a corner ... and wrote her name into Australian football folklore.

Katie Zelem, Manchester United vs. Leicester City | 2021-22 Women's Super League

Scoring one Olimpico is hard enough, but Zelem managed to do it twice in one game. What's more, Zelem scored an Olimpico in the match before this one too.

Katie McCabe, Republic of Ireland vs. Canada | 2023 Women's World Cup

In their first appearance at a Women's World Cup, captain McCabe made sure Ireland fans would never forget the tournament with this inspirational strike.

Christian Pulisic, AC Milan vs. Club Brugge | 2024-25 UEFA Champions League

USMNT star Pulisic called it "a bit of luck" at the time, but there's no doubting the quality of his strike for AC Milan in their 3-1 win over Club Brugge in last season's Champions League league phase.

Son Heung-Min, Tottenham Hotspur vs. Manchester United | 2024-25 Carabao Cup

No Olimpico list would be complete without Son's stunner that sent Manchester United packing in the 2024-25 Carabao Cup quarterfinals. The South Korea skipper's crazy 88th-minute strike was the perfect denouement of a topsy-turvy match that finished 4-3 after Spurs had been leading 3-0.

Ángel Di María, Rosario Central vs. Boca Juniors | 2025 Liga Profesional de Fútbol

Last, but certainly not least, is this beauty from Di María for Rosario Central in their 1-1 draw with Boca Juniors in September. The Argentina star has a habit of scoring from corners, with this one -- astonishingly -- his fourth Olimpico.

stories.headline: Tom Brady tops list of athletes who became owners
stories.summary: The legendary quarterback is a member of an exclusive list of athletes that includes LeBron James, Serena Williams and Wayne Gretzky.
stories.body:
Tom Brady is getting (back) into the ownership game.

On Friday, sources confirmed to ESPN and NFL Network that the former superstar quarterback had bought shares in the English soccer giants Chelsea. Brady's purchasing of Chelsea shares comes after he departed the ownership group of another English club, EFL Championship side Birmingham City, earlier in the month after originally becoming a minority owner with a 3.3% stake.

Brady's latest interest isn't his only foray into the world of ownership -- he also owns a 5% minority stake in the Las Vegas Raiders, purchased in 2024, and he also has a stake in the Las Vegas Aces.

The NFL legend is far from the first athlete, active or former, to enter the ownership sphere. Here are other athletes who are now team owners:

Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Atlético Madrid

In October 26 news broke that the star Oklahoma City Thunder guard would be joining the club as an investor.

"I am excited to officially join the group of shareholders of Atlético de Madrid," Gilgeous-Alexander said in the club's post. "This is a club with a long history at the top of European football, and I am grateful for the opportunity to be part of its future."

Jason Kidd -- Everton

In April 2025, English Premier League club Everton announced that then-Dallas Mavericks coach Jason Kidd would be adding a different title to his résumé: ownership group member. The news came after Kidd joined Roundhouse Capital Holdings, which is part of the Friedkin Group -- the U.S. firm that completed its takeover of Everton's ownership the previous December.

Vince Carter, Tracy McGrady, Jozy Altidore -- Buffalo Bills

In December 2024, the Bills announced Carter, McGrady and Altidore were among 10 limited partners the team was adding to its ownership group. Both McGrady (New York Knicks) and Altidore (New York Red Bulls) played for New York-area teams, while Carter spent time with the Brooklyn Nets (who were known as the New Jersey Nets at the time) and was McGrady's teammate on the Toronto Raptors (who are closer to Buffalo than NYC-based teams).

Tom Brady -- Las Vegas Aces, Las Vegas Raiders, Chelsea

The Las Vegas Aces, the reigning WNBA champions, have added to their championship credentials. Seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady acquired a minority stake in the team whose majority owner is Las Vegas Raiders owner Mark Davis.

"I have always been a huge fan of women's sports, and I admire the work that the Aces' players, staff, and the WNBA continue to do to grow the sport and empower future generations of athletes," Brady said in a statement. "To be able to contribute in any way to that mission as a member of the Aces organization is an incredible honor."

Brady attended an Aces game in May 2022 and sent gifts to star Kelsey Plum. Plum and other Aces players were excited to have Brady as part of the team.

He also added the Las Vegas Raiders to his resume after his purchase of minority stake in the franchise was approved by NFL teams owners on Tuesday. The deal was agreed on in May 2023, but it took owners 17 months to give their approval over concerns he was receiving too much of a discount from majority owner Mark Davis.

Brady was also a minority owner of Birmingham City, a club in English soccer's second-tier Championship, but sold his shares in November 2026. He purchased shares in Chelsea later that month.

Lewis Hamilton -- Denver Broncos

The Broncos' ownership group added racing royalty in August 2022. Formula One driver Lewis Hamilton has a stake with the Walton-Penner group, which purchased the team in June 2022.

Hamilton, 37, has the Formula One record for most race wins and has won the Formula One title seven times. The ownership group, which purchased the team for $4.65 billion, is led by Walmart heir Rob Walton and includes former U.S. Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice, who also has a stake.

In April, Hamilton joined with Serena Williams in a consortium led by former Liverpool chairman Martin Broughton in an attempt to buy Premier League club Chelsea.

"He is a champion competitor who knows what it takes to lead a winning team," Walton said in a statement.

Marshawn Lynch -- Seattle Kraken

Lynch spent 13 seasons in Seattle with the Seahawks, but his new sports venture in the state of Washington is on the ice. On April 18, he joined the Seattle Kraken ownership team as a minority investor. The former NFL running back will be a part of the NHL's "Hockey is for Everyone" campaign and Kraken owner Tod Leiweke said Lynch expressed interest in shadowing him to learn hockey CEO operations.

"This is something I never would have imagined," Lynch said to CNBC in a statement. "I always dreamed of playing on a professional team but owning one is something special. As I look back on some of my accomplishments...I'm [going to] continue to count my blessings."

Grammy Award-winning artist and Seattle native Macklemore also joined the Kraken ownership team with Lynch.

Wayne Gretzky, Steve Nash and Dustin Johnson -- Las Vegas Desert Dogs

Wayne Gretzky is a big lacrosse guy? Yep, you read that right. The Great One may have made his name on the ice, but before Gretzky was the pride of the Edmonton Oilers he was a bona fide lax bro.

"The national sport of Canada is box lacrosse," Gretzky said. "I started playing lacrosse on a team at the age of six and played all the way until I was 16 years old. I have a great love for the game in the sense I really think that box lacrosse was such a crucial part of the success I ultimately had in ice hockey."

Because of this, it shouldn't be completely surprising that the hockey legend is linking up with 2020 Masters champion Dustin Johnson, NBA Hall of Famer and current Brooklyn Nets head coach Steve Nash and Nets owner Joe Tsai as part of a star-studded ownership group for the National Lacrosse League's newest expansion team in Las Vegas, the Desert Dogs.

Dwyane Wade -- Utah Jazz

Seeing Dwyane Wade support any team other than the Miami Heat is decidedly jarring. In April, the three-time NBA champion purchased an ownership stake in the Utah Jazz, joining majority owner and team governor Ryan Smith, and expressed a desire to take an active role in the franchise. D. Wade made good on his promise. He could be seen courtside throughout the season; he took action when an unsettling fan incident went down during the postseason, and he became a mentor to then-Jazz star Donovan Mitchell.

The former Miami Heat star also added to his portfolio with something a bit closer to home. Wade, a Chicago native, joined the ownership group of the WNBA's Chicago Sky.

"It's a great opportunity to be a part of the league in its very early stages. ... Growth is going to happen, and so I want to be a part of the growth of this league," Wade said.

Kevin Durant -- Philadelphia Union, NJ/NY Gotham FC

In June 2020, Brooklyn Nets star Kevin Durant purchased a 5% stake in MLS' Philadelphia Union, and he has an option to purchase an additional 5% at a later date. Durant also had engaged in talks about purchasing part of D.C. United the year prior, but he said the discussion never progressed.

Durant expanded his portfolio in May of this year, after being named as a minority owner of the National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) club NJ/NY Gotham FC.

Thirty Five Ventures (35V), a company co-founded by the two-time NBA champion and entrepreneur Rich Kleiman, made a significant investment to acquire a stake in the club, marking the company's second investment in a professional soccer team.

Renee Montgomery -- Atlanta Dream

Former Atlanta Dream guard Renee Montgomery made history in February as part of a three-member investor group that was approved to purchase the team. Montgomery is the first former player to become both an owner and executive of a WNBA franchise. The ownership change followed pressure on former Republican Sen. Kelly Loeffler to sell her share of the Dream, after she angered WNBA players with her opposition to the league's racial justice initiatives.

Patrick Mahomes -- Kansas City Royals

Patrick Mahomes is no stranger to winning. While the Kansas City Royals can't exactly say the same, you can't rule out that the quarterback's winning ways might rub off on the franchise now that he is part of their ownership group. If Mahomes' status as an icon in Kansas City was in question (it wasn't), this move surely cemented it. Becoming a baseball owner made sense on several levels for the Chiefs' QB1. Not only was Mahomes -- who played baseball in college -- a legitimate pro prospect, his father, Pat Mahomes, spent 11 seasons in Major League Baseball. He also had to find some way to put that $503 million contract extension to good use.

Venus and Serena Williams -- Miami Dolphins, Angel City FC

Winning major titles and making history, that's what the Williams sisters do. In 2009, Venus and Serena became the first Black female minority owners in the NFL by purchasing a part of the Miami Dolphins. Musicians Jimmy Buffett, Gloria and Emilio Estefan, Fergie and Marc Anthony also bought shares in the team -- the Dolphins' ownership group is nothing if not eclectic. Then, last year, Serena Williams became part of the star-studded Angel City FC ownership group bringing a NWSL team to Los Angeles in 2022.

Mia Hamm, Abby Wambach and Julie Foudy -- Angel City FC

When Angel City FC arrived on the scene it did so in style. Before we even knew the Los Angeles based NWSL club's name, we knew it had superstar backing like no other. Among the 14 former USWNT players who are part of the group are Mia Hamm, Abby Wambach and Julie Foudy. I would have named Lauren Holiday, Shannon Boxx, Rachel Buehler, Amanda Cromwell, Joy Fawcett, Tisha Venturini Hoch, Angela Hucles, Shannon MacMillan, Saskia Webber and sisters Lorrie Fair Allen and Ronnie Fair Sullins, but I was really trying to stay true to my whole "I'm only going to name 20 athletes" thing from the intro. There are also a bunch of celebrities in the mix, but we don't have that kind of time.

Michael Jordan -- Charlotte Hornets

While we're on the subject of owners who haven't had the type of success we grew accustomed to in their playing days, I would be remiss if I didn't mention the GOAT. In 2010, Michael Jordan became the first ex-player to be a majority owner in the league when the NBA's Board of Governors unanimously approved his $275 million bid to buy the then Charlotte Bobcats in his home state of North Carolina. After a decade of underwhelming years, things look to be on the up for the now Hornets with Rookie of the Year LaMelo Ball providing a long-awaited spark in the organization. Never forget when his dad said he could beat MJ one-on-one ... good times.

Alex Rodriguez -- Minnesota Timberwolves, Minnesota Lynx

I don't know what part of this purchase feels less ideal to me, that Alex Rodriguez and his 50-50 business partner Marc Lore are only pursuing acquiring the Minnesota Timberwolves and Lynx after their original plan to buy the New York Mets failed or that Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards had no idea who former MLB star A-Rod was. Either way, the $1.5 billion deal is expected to close around July 1.

David Beckham -- Inter Miami

David Beckham, iconic soccer player and remains-to-be-seen owner. Beckham -- who is incredibly hands on with the franchise -- is part of an ownership group which was initially called Miami Beckham United but now operates under the name Miami Freedom Park LLC. Beckham and Inter Miami have seemingly been riddled with controversy since the club's inception in 2018. But all those problems could be a thing of the past if Lionel Messi decides to head to MLS. Hey, stranger things have happened.

LeBron James -- Liverpool

Back in 2011, LeBron James and manager Maverick Carter became minority owners of Premier League club Liverpool after Fenway Sports Group, which purchased the team in 2010, became the sole marketer of James' global rights. The deal has turned out to be pretty lucrative for James -- his original stake in the club, valued at about $6.5 million, had grown to about $32 million as of 2018. In 2019, Liverpool won the Premier League for their first top-flight league title in thirty years.

James Harden -- Houston Dynamo, Houston Dash

James Harden might not be in Houston anymore, but the former Rockets superstar's presence is still felt in the city. The Beard purchased a 5% stake in the group that controls MLS' Houston Dynamo and NWSL's Houston Dash in 2019. Boxer Oscar De La Hoya is also part of the group. The Dash won their first NWSL title last year, so he's probably feeling pretty good about that investment.

Russell Wilson and Ken Griffey Jr. -- Seattle Sounders

What do Russell Wilson, Ken Griffey Jr. and Macklemore have in common? They are all part of the Seattle Sounders' ownership group. Wilson, along with his wife, musician Ciara, purchased a stake in the team in 2019 -- just in time for them to win an MLS Cup title. Griffey Jr. and his family followed suit in November 2020.

Zlatan Ibrahimovic -- Hammaraby

Seemingly everything Zlatan does makes people react intensely, and that remained true when he purchased part of Swedish team Hammaraby back in 2019. Fans of Malmo, another Swedish team where Zlatan started his professional career, reacted by vandalizing a statue of Zlatan outside the team's home stadium, placing a toilet seat around one of its arms.

Magic Johnson -- Los Angeles Dodgers

Big LA guy. In 2012, Lakers great Magic Johnson was part of a group that bought the Los Angeles Dodgers from Frank McCourt for a record $2 billion. At the time, the price shattered the mark for a sports franchise. Magic kept it real at the time of purchase when explaining his role in recruiting free agents, saying that while he can't talk hitting or pitching with players, he "can talk winning." If recent history is any indication (in case you blacked out all of 2020 -- the Dodgers won the World Series), it worked.

stories.headline: Kangaroos bounce Kiwis for fourth-straight Rugby League World Cup title
stories.summary: The Kangaroos have won a fourth-straight Rugby League World Cup, toppling New Zealand 32-12 in Brisbane.
stories.body:
The Kangaroos have punished a disappointing New Zealand, with Reece Walsh running riot in a 32-12 World Cup final waltz.

There was an expectation the Kiwis, searching for their second Cup title and first since 2008, would push Australia all the way after a two-point loss in a pulsating tournament opener.

But the visitors struggled from the outset in Brisbane on Sunday night, Jamayne Isaako's kick-off floating long in a sign of things to come.

Walsh dazzled at fullback for the Kangaroos, his pace, vision and wicked footwork too much as he helped lay on two tries and generally wreak havoc around the ruck and close to the line.

Conversely, Walsh's New Zealand opposite Kalyn Ponga -- International Rugby League's Golden Boot winner on Thursday night -- was unable to get into game.

Australian hooker Harry Grant and halves Tom Dearden and Cam Munster completely outplayed their error-riddled opposites, while the Kangaroos' pack muscled up.

Dearden laid on two first-half tries for Liam Martin with well-timed short balls, while Bradman Best was rewarded for an inspired chase-down tackle of Jahrome Hughes with a try soon after.

When Tom Trbojevic scored to begin the second half it was 28-6 and effectively game over.

Jack Bostock completed his breakout season with a try in each half for Australia.

It was the Kangaroos' fourth consecutive title and 10th in the last 11 tournaments, dating back to 1975.

stories.headline: Judging overreactions to NFL Week 11: Joe Brady's Bills impact, Eagles' chances
stories.summary: Is Brady the coach that can vault the Bills over the top? Is an NFC East three-peat still in play in Philly? We overreact to Week 11 NFL action.
stories.body:
After watching the Thursday night game, I was all set to do a "The Colts need to cut Daniel Jones" item for the Week 11 overreactions column, but Indianapolis went ahead and beat me to it. I'm not sure it would have been an overreaction by me, and I'm not sure it was an overreaction by the Colts.

We are entering the fish-or-cut-bait time of the year in the NFL. Thanksgiving is in four days. December starts next week. At this point, if something isn't working, we're past the time for patience. If you're still in the race, every move you make must be about what could make the difference in your favor. If you're out of it, every move needs to be about figuring out the plan for 2027 and beyond. The Colts concluded that they weren't going anywhere with Jones and it was time to get another look at Anthony Richardson Sr. And no one who watched the first game of Week 11 could accuse them overreacting.

Then came Sunday, which brought us a sixth straight Ravens loss, the merciful end of a seven-game Eagles losing streak, three Jeffery Simmons sacks in a Bears victory that set up a Thanksgiving showdown between a pair of 8-2 NFC North teams and another Cowboys game in which the total went over 80 points. And that was all just in the early window.

Let's look at five potential takeaways from all the Week 11 action and judge them as legitimate stances or irrational stretches. Plus, we hit a few fantasy football overreactions at the end.

Jump to:

Bills made right call by hiring Joe Brady?

Eagles still can win NFC East?

Young only NFC South QB to return in 2027?

Pickens to return to Cowboys on extension?

Mendoza is already the AFC West's QB2?

Fantasy overreactions

The Bills made the right move replacing Sean McDermott with Joe Brady
Buffalo won again Sunday, beating the Dolphins 26-9 to improve to 9-1, which is the best record in the league at this writing. (The 49ers can match it with a win Sunday night over the Vikings.) It wasn't Josh Allen's best game -- he posted a 28.9 QBR thanks to a pair of interceptions and tried to reset the balance of the universe a bit by handing the ball off to James Cook III for a 1-yard touchdown instead of collecting another for himself. But it was good enough to beat woeful Miami, especially with the help of a Buffalo defense that hasn't allowed a touchdown since Nov. 1.

Verdict: NOT AN OVERREACTION

The Bills surprised a lot of people by moving on from the highly successful McDermott last January after losing in overtime in the divisional round of the playoffs last year, elevating offensive coordinator Brady. But so far, it's tough to argue with the results. Brady has preached an "all gas, no brakes" mentality, trying to maintain urgency from the beginning and make it clear that his team has the highest of high hopes for this season.

His best decision might have been hiring Jim Leonhard as defensive coordinator. Buffalo's defense hasn't been the best in the league, but it's been a heck of a lot better in November than it was in September and October, indicating that the Bills needed time to grow into the new scheme. The disclaimer is that the Bills have played the Jets and Dolphins the last two weeks and only have three wins over teams which currently have winning records.

Buffalo gets the Chiefs on Thursday night, then goes on the road to New England and Green Bay before returning home to play the Bears. The Bills then head to Denver on Christmas Day, so the upcoming schedule represents a tougher test than what they've been facing. But 9-1 is 9-1, and right now it looks like Brady is pushing the right buttons.

The Eagles are still in the NFC East race
As mentioned, Philadelphia snapped a seven-game losing streak Sunday with a gritty 19-16 victory over the Steelers in the Pennsylvania state championship game. It's tough to lose seven games in a row and say with a straight face that you're still in your division race, but it's not completely ridiculous in the NFC East. The win improved Philly's record to 3-7, which puts it 3.5 games behind the first-place Giants after New York's 23-18 victory over Jacksonville on Sunday.

The Eagles lost their first meeting of the season with the Giants but get them again in the final game of the season. Other than that, their only remaining opponents that currently have winning records are the Seahawks and 49ers. Fill-in QB Joe Milton had a do-no-harm game, Saquon Barkley rushed for 75 yards and a long touchdown, and the Eagles' defense sacked Aaron Rodgers five times while holding the Steelers to 255 total yards. If they can beat Dallas on Thanksgiving, the Eagles would only be a half-game behind the second-place Cowboys and still within shouting distance of Big Blue. You never know in the NFC East.

Verdict: OVERREACTION

Holding the Steelers to 255 yards sounds nice until you realize the Eagles managed a mere 214 yards themselves on only 50 offensive plays. It's not every week that they're going to get to face a 42-year-old quarterback who averages less than four yards per attempt and whose nominal top wide receiver gets thrown out of the game after racking up two receiving yards on one catch.

Pittsburgh's leading receiver in this game was a person named Max Hurleman, who caught six passes for 61 receiving yards to raise his career totals to ... six catches and 61 receiving yards. Their leading rusher was, incredibly, Rodgers, who had 29 yards on five panicked carries. The Eagles' opponent Thursday has Dak Prescott throwing to CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. Safe to assume the Eagles are going to need more than 214 yards to win that one.

Look, it's a shame what's happened to the Eagles, who are playing without injured starting QB Jalen Hurts, multiple members of their Week 1 starting offensive line and with a banged-up Barkley and DeVonta Smith. But it's hard to imagine they have the firepower to stay in the race, even in that division.

Bryce Young is the only NFC South quarterback who will be back as his team's starter next season
The Panthers won a doozy, beating the Ravens 35-33 in a game that wasn't decided until a tipped-ball interception in the final minutes. Young was 22-for-30 for 254 passing yards, two touchdown passes and an interception. The game helped break him out of a slump, as his QBR had been under 50 in four of his previous five games, but it was also Carolina's second win in a row and improved the Panthers' record to 5-5 -- good enough for a two-game lead in the NFC South.

Meanwhile, Tyler Shough and the Saints couldn't get anything going against the Bears in Chicago, Baker Mayfield played through injury in a loss to the Lions and the 3-7 Falcons took the week off in the hopes that Michael Penix Jr. will play better post-bye than he has for the past month. The records -- and QB situations -- in the NFC South are not the best.

Verdict: OVERREACTION

Do we even know for sure if Young will be back as Carolina's starter next year? Sure, if the Panthers finish over .500 and win the division, you'd think so. But he hasn't made himself inevitable by any stretch. The Panthers, Falcons and Saints are still hoping but are unsure whether they have their long-term answer at QB. The Bucs? Well, Mayfield has $50 million in guaranteed salary owed to him next year, so things would have to go really bad for them to move on from him.

The potential for new coaching staffs in Tampa Bay, New Orleans and Carolina certainly calls some things into question, and the fact that the Falcons' staff is in its first year and inherited Penix means he might not be on solid ground, either. But that $50 million makes me think Mayfield is back in Tampa at the very least.

George Pickens is going to get a monster contract from the Cowboys this offseason
Yeah, the Cowboys scored touchdowns on each of their first six possessions in Sunday's 51-30 victory over Tennessee. Pickens scored one of those and finished with 102 receiving yards on seven catches. Over the past two weeks, he has 18 catches for 247 receiving yards and four touchdowns and the Cowboys have scored 91 points to go 1-1. Pickens had 1,429 receiving yards and nine touchdowns on 93 catches last season, his first with Dallas, and has clearly established himself as an elite, No. 1-type wide receiver since linking up with Prescott in the Cowboys' high-octane offense. He's playing on a $27.298 million franchise tag this year, and it would cost Dallas $32.7576 million to franchise him again in 2027.

Verdict: OVERREACTION

The Cowboys could have signed Pickens this past offseason if they wanted to. They made it clear early on that they did not. They wanted to see more than one great season before committing long-term. After a bit of a slow start, he's having one. Problem is, they still have Lamb and are scheduled to pay him $29 million next year. If Pickens is looking for mid-to-high $30 millions for an average on his next deal, it's going to be tough to pay them both.

And, by the way, Lamb had 132 receiving yards and a touchdown on 11 catches Sunday. It's not as if they don't already have a No. 1 wide receiver. The prediction here is that the Cowboys either let Pickens hit the market or franchise him with the intention of working out a trade.

Fernando Mendoza is the second-best QB in the AFC West right now!
After rushing for a touchdown in his first NFL start last week, Mendoza threw his first three NFL touchdown passes Sunday in a 38-24 Raiders loss in Denver. He has not looked remotely overwhelmed or like the game is too big for him. He played the entirety of Sunday's game and most of last week's game without his best receiver, injured tight end Brock Bowers. He's brought Ashton Jeanty back to life, for goodness' sake.

He had the Raiders in this game, despite the heroic efforts of Broncos rookie running back Jonah Coleman, until the final two minutes. Mendoza had the ball with a chance to drive and tie the game before Broncos corner Ja'Quan McMillian made a brilliant interception and returned it for a game-sealing touchdown right after two-minute warning.

Mendoza plays on a team whose defense has now allowed 30 or more points in seven of its 11 games this season. If you're grading on a curve, you must give Mendoza high marks for his first two NFL starts. If you're just trusting your eyes, you have to say that he has a chance to be fun at the very least.

Verdict: OVERREACTION

I mean, Mendoza lost Sunday's game to Bo Nix, even if his individual performance was better than Nix's was. And Justin Herbert had one of his best games of this season Sunday, which isn't saying much, but again, like Nix ... he's made more than two NFL starts.

Would it be a surprise if we could make the case for Mendoza as the division's second-best QB behind Patrick Mahomes this time next year? Not entirely. But not quite yet either. Let's enjoy what we're seeing and look forward to watching the No. 1 overall pick continue to thrive and develop as a quarterback, a press conference legend and a pretty good insurance commercial actor. Young man has a lot on his plate!

Quick-hitter fantasy overreactions

Cam Ward is worth adding in all keeper leagues. NOT AN OVERREACTION. He was the first pick in the real draft, so he kind of should be, right? The Titans have surrounded Ward with a good mix of young and veteran skill talent, and he's improving as his first season with Brian Daboll moves along. Worth a speculative add, for sure.
Justice Hill is a must-add if you roster Derrick Henry. NOT AN OVERREACTION. I mean, maybe even if you don't. The Ravens are probably going to be playing from behind a fair bit, and Hill seems like the guy who gets the ball when they are.

You need to trade Ashton Jeanty right now off this huge week. OVERREACTION. You've come this far! As ugly as it's been, Jeanty has retained fantasy value as a pass-catcher, and Fernando Mendoza looks like the real deal. Plus, the schedule the rest of the way isn't bad (other than that Week 13 bye). He gets Arizona in Week 17!!!
Every Cowboys skill-position player is a must-start. NOT AN OVERREACTION. Dallas is fantasy gold right now. Start Prescott. Start Lamb. Start Pickens. Start Javonte Williams. Heck, start Ryan Flournoy. The Cowboys offense is a machine, and the Cowboys' defense is going to keep them in shootouts.
Max Hurleman should be a good flex option moving forward. OVERREACTION. We have ESPN Research checking to see if this is a fan who won a contest.

stories.headline: Fantasy baseball: Breaking down Tarik Skubal's fantasy value on the Mets
stories.summary: What Tarik Skubal signing a nine-year deal with the Mets means for his fantasy value.
stories.body:
Two winters ago, the New York Mets opened their wallet to get their offensive centerpiece, Juan Soto. On Sunday, the Mets did the same to get a centerpiece for their rotation, and for a similarly record-setting deal, signing Tarik Skubal to a nine-year, $450 million contract.

Fortunately for us in fantasy, we won't need to spend as much as the Mets did to add Skubal to our rosters, but it's a good landing spot for the lefty. He'll call one of the more pitching-leaning ballparks in Citi Field his home through 2036.

Recent dominance
Skubal's back-to-back Cy Young campaigns of 2024-25 represented the peak of a lengthy stay at the top of the fantasy baseball pitching ranks. In fact, that extended stretch of greatness (spanning games from July 4, 2023, through April 29, 2026) saw him post major league leading totals in wins (41) and WHIP (0.91). He also placed top-five in quality starts (53, 3rd), ERA (2.41, second among those with at least 50 starts) and strikeout rate (31.2%, fifth). Skubal's 1,463 fantasy points scored during that time span were 258 more than the next-closest pitcher.

No other pitcher has had multiple 550-plus-point fantasy seasons since the COVID-shortened 2020. Skubal's were consecutive (2024-25) and he is the first pitcher to do that in back-to-back years since Gerrit Cole, Jacob deGrom and Justin Verlander all did it in both 2018 and 2019.

And that's not to suggest that Skubal has fallen from said peak. Following his trade to the Los Angeles Dodgers at the deadline last year, Skubal's 161 fantasy points scored were only 16 off the lead among pitchers, and he was top-five in the majors in quality starts (7, tied for third) and strikeouts (70, t-3rd) with highly competitive numbers in terms of ERA (2.61), WHIP (1.05) and K% (28.5%).

But the cause of the endpoint of the aforementioned stretch of dominance -- that being, injuries -- largely remain the only concern surrounding Skubal. He underwent surgery in May to remove loose bodies from his elbow, missing 38 games, and he has had two prior arm operations, a Tommy John surgery in 2017 while in college and flexor tendon surgery that cost him a significant chunk of 2022.

That said, Skubal's return after a mere 43-day stint on the injured list this past summer, after which time he posted a 2.71 ERA, 0.97 WHIP and 31.2% strikeout percentage while not missing a single start when including the postseason, demonstrated his otherwise near-infallible ability. Those rates were well within range of his combined numbers from his Cy Young years (2.39 ERA, 0.92 WHIP, 30.3 K%).

No. 1 starting pitcher and top-five overall

In signing with the Mets -- and for that amount of money -- Skubal will need to first pass his pre-signing physical, a step which presumably would bring any immediate and/or serious concerns about his health to light.

Any inherent risk is well worth taking in Skubal's case, especially considering the already risky nature of every front-line starting pitcher in this era. Cam Schlittler and Jacob Misiorowski are both coming off their first-ever seasons as Cy Young-caliber starters, and both saw more than 40-inning jumps (postseason included) from 2025-26. Cristopher Sanchez's skills dipped slightly after the All-Star break. Yoshinobu Yamamoto's volume tends to be reined in by the Los Angeles Dodgers' fluid pitching rotation plans, while Chris Sale's workload was heavily monitored by the Atlanta Braves, which makes sense considering his 37 years of age.

Skubal remains both my No. 1 full-time fantasy starting pitcher -- Shohei Ohtani's hitting contributions coupled with his positional eligibility technically place him atop the list -- and a clear-cut, top-five overall selection in early ESPN standard league drafts. In rotisserie formats, he's a legitimate first-round pick, dependent upon your overall pitching strategy (many managers will not invest their first selection on a pitcher, though it is an entirely defensible position).

That's highly unlikely to change without some sort of signal to the contrary once the anticipated lockout gets resolved and we get further details and reports out of whatever length spring training we get.

stories.headline: Reports: Dynamo's Herrera charged with DWI, club aware of 'incident'
stories.summary: Houston Dynamo FC midfielder Héctor Herrera was charged with driving while intoxicated on Saturday in Montgomery County, Texas, according to multiple reports.
stories.body:
Houston Dynamo FC midfielder Héctor Herrera was charged with driving while intoxicated on Saturday in Montgomery County, Texas, according to multiple reports.

MLS and the Houston Dynamo said in a statement to ESPN on Sunday that they are looking into an "incident" involving Herrera.

"The Houston Dynamo are aware of an incident involving Héctor Herrera on Friday night. The Club and Major League Soccer are working to gather additional information," said the Dynamo's statement to ESPN. "We will refrain from providing further comment until appropriate."

The Dynamo are set to begin a best-of-three playoff series against the San Jose Earthquakes on Nov. 24. It is unclear whether Herrera will be available for the match.

The situation could mark another misstep for Herrera, who was sent off in 2024 for spitting on a referee. Following the event, the Dynamo denied his 2025 contract extension, before bringing him back for the 2026 season.

Between 2022 to 2024, Herrera made 69 appearances (including playoffs) for the Dynamo. The Pachuca academy product then made his way to Liga MX's Toluca in 2025, where he won the Clausura and Apertura titles in Mexico's top-flight.

Since his return to Houston in 2026, Herrera has made 30 appearances across the regular season. The midfielder has three goals and two assists this year.

Spotrac's Caleb Pongratz was the first to report the news and the Houston Chronicle published a story Sunday with confirmation of the charge from the Montgomery County sheriff's office.

stories.headline: Alexander-Walker has 27 points as Hawks roll to 107-97 win over Pistons in off game for Cunningham
stories.summary: — Nickeil Alexander-Walker scored 27 points, Atlanta opened the fourth quarter with an 18-0 run, and the Hawks beat the Detroit Pistons 107-97 on Sunday as Cade Cunningham was held to a season-low five points.
stories.body:
ATLANTA -- — Nickeil Alexander-Walker scored 27 points, Atlanta opened the fourth quarter with an 18-0 run, and the Hawks beat the Detroit Pistons 107-97 on Sunday as Cade Cunningham was held to a season-low five points.


Cunningham set a season high with 15 assists but a combination of early foul trouble and a sore knee combined to hold him to 20 points below his average of 25.6 as he made 2 of 9 shots. It was his first game of the season not scoring in double figures.


Corey Kispert scored a season-high 18 points and Lu Dort had 16 in the Hawks' fourth straight win.


Isaiah Joe led Detroit with 19 points. Ausar Thompson and John Collins had 18 and Paul Reed added 16.


The Pistons led 85-74 at the start of the fourth quarter before the Hawks took a 92-85 with the 18 unanswered points. Joe's 3-pointer with 4:52 remaining ended Detroit's scoreless streak.


Cunningham picked up two fouls in the first period and was called for his third foul early in the second. He was limited to 14 minutes in the first half while missing all three of his shots from the field.


Cunningham scored his first points with a jumper off the glass early in the second half but continued to focus on setting up shots for teammates while receiving extra defensive attention from Dyson Daniels and the Hawks.


Cunningham was included on Detroit's injury report with right knee soreness. Coach J.B. Bickerstaff said before the game protecting Cunningham was “the most important thing. He’s a competitor and wants to play. But it’s also our responsibility to just make sure that we’re protecting him at all costs.”


Cunningham was held out of Detroit's 122-109 win at New Orleans on Wednesday night but scored 23 points in a 105-102 loss to Toronto on Friday night.


Hawks rookie Kingston Flemings had 10 points after missing three games with a sore back.


Up next
Pistons: Play at Orlando on Tuesday night.


Hawks: Visit Boston on Friday night.
